title: fix(driver-sql): a boolean retyped from text stores 1 / 0 on SQLite, so a saved false no longer reads as true
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Ca1jJvsA1dHsPwMiQb
Fixes #35341

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：在 SQLite 上，把字段类型从「文本」改成「是/否」之后，存「否」的记录现在读出来就是「否」，列表、去重、分组和「= 否」筛选结果一致；以前存成怪写法的老记录会在下次启动时自动纠正。
- 为什么做：这类字段过去每次保存「否」都被存成「0.0」，读出来却显示「是」，筛选和显示互相矛盾，用户看到的是/否值是错的。
- 出错会怎样：只影响 SQLite 上改过类型的是/否字段；新建的是/否字段存储形式不变。若启动时纠正失败，只会记一条警告并在下次启动重试，不会阻止启动。
- 要你做什么：无，席位落地。

## 席位核对

- Where to look first: `sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts` (the new `sqliteBooleanBinding` and its use at the end of `formatInput`), then the comparand branch at the top of `coerceFilterValue` in `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts`, then the widened `SQLITE_LEGACY_BOOLEAN_TEXT` and the `UPDATE` in `backfillCanonicalBooleans` (`sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`).
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/sql-driver-35341-retyped-boolean-text-column.test.ts` answers 11/11 green; the CONTROL describe (a boolean column the driver created) shows the integer `1` / `0` storage unchanged.
- Route: B (the card's Ask), no read-side backstop. Reason: binding the write and the comparand as the text `'1'` / `'0'` and extending the boot convergence to `'1.0'` / `'0.0'` makes `find()`, `distinct()` and `= false` agree on new and existing rows, so `presentStoredBoolean` needs no widening (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 12) and the stored form converges on one spelling, the direction of PR #35076.

## What changes

On SQLite, a `text` field retyped to `boolean` keeps its TEXT column. knex's better-sqlite3 client binds a JS boolean as `Number(b)`, better-sqlite3 binds a JS number as a REAL, and TEXT affinity keeps the REAL as the text `'0.0'` / `'1.0'`, which `presentStoredBoolean` read as `true` both.

- **Write.** `formatInput` (SQLite only) binds a declared scalar boolean (`booleanFields`) that holds a JS boolean as the text `'1'` / `'0'` (`sqliteBooleanBinding`). NUMERIC affinity (a column the driver created) folds it into the INTEGER `1` / `0`, unchanged from before; TEXT affinity keeps `'1'` / `'0'`, the spelling the boot convergence writes and the presenter reads. Every write door runs through `formatInput`: create, update, upsert, bulkCreate, bulkUpdate, updateMany.
- **Comparand.** `coerceFilterValue` binds a boolean comparand on the same fields the same way, so `= false` / `= true` / `$in` / `$ne` select the rows the row read presents as that boolean.
- **Existing rows.** `SQLITE_LEGACY_BOOLEAN_TEXT` (the backfill's count, sample, `UPDATE` and the `os migrate plan` preview all read it) now also selects `'1.0'` / `'0.0'`, and the `UPDATE` maps them to `1` / `0`. They were counted as withheld and warned about before.
- A BigInt would bind an INTEGER too; it is not used because knex's query-text formatter throws on one (measured: `str.replace is not a function`).

## Acceptance notes

- The data door was measured, before and after (todo example on a better-sqlite3 file database, a field booted as `text` then retyped to `boolean`; the example edit was a scratch edit, reverted, not in this diff). See Verification.
- driver-sqlite-wasm and driver-turso inherit `isSqlite` and so take the same bind. sql.js already bound an integer-valued number as INTEGER, so a TEXT column there stored `'0'` before this change and stores `'0'` after; this was reasoned from sql.js's binder, not measured here.
- A number `0` / `1` (not a JS boolean) handed straight to the driver is not rebound; the engine's boolean arm hands the driver JS booleans.

## Verification

<details><summary>A0, the REST data door, origin/main 6f36818f03 vs this branch</summary>

Before (origin/main): after the retype boot, `pragma_table_info` reads `probe_flag` TEXT. `POST /api/v1/data/todo_task` with `probe_flag: false` answers 201 with `"probe_flag":true`; the cell is the text `'0.0'` (and `'1.0'` for true). The list reads both rows as `true`; the `probe_flag = false` filter returns the false row, presented as `true`.

After (driver-sql rebuilt at af25ec33ef, same database file): the boot rewrote the two rows to `'0'` / `'1'`. `POST` with `false` answers `"probe_flag":false` and stores `'0'`. The list reads `[door_false,false],[door_true,true],[post_false,false],[post_true,true]`; the `= false` filter returns exactly `door_false` and `post_false`, both `false`.
</details>

<details><summary>A1 to A3, measured on origin/main 6f36818f03 at the driver</summary>

- A1: knex 3.3.0 `client-better-sqlite3` `_formatBindings` maps a boolean to `Number(b)`; better-sqlite3 13.0.3 binds it as REAL. On the retyped TEXT column, create, update, bulkCreate and updateMany all stored `'0.0'` / `'1.0'`; on an INTEGER-form column, `0` / `1`.
- A2: `backfillCanonicalBooleans` writes the integer `1` / `0`, which a TEXT column stores as the text `'1'` / `'0'`. `'0.0'` / `'1.0'` were not in its population: a reboot logged `left 7 row(s) of ... unconverted` and changed nothing.
- A3: `presentStoredBoolean` reads `'false'` / `'0'` as false, `'true'` / `'1'` as true, anything else as `Boolean(value)`, so `'0.0'` reads `true`. The `= false` comparand bound as REAL compared as `'0.0'` on the TEXT column: it matched the `'0.0'` rows and missed the `'0'` row the convergence left.
</details>
